<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=39220 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
Thanks for reporting the Docker persistence problem. This automated hermes-sweeper review verified that current `main` now preserves the WhatsApp bridge dependency directory on the durable data volume.

- `491579fa05eff16767dd25ca6c29e755b1141fd9` (`fix(whatsapp): resolve bridge dir with HERMES_HOME mirror in Docker`, shipped in `v2026.7.1`) makes a read-only `/opt/hermes` bridge resolve to `$HERMES_HOME/scripts/whatsapp-bridge` instead (`gateway/platforms/whatsapp_common.py:464-508`).
- The WhatsApp adapter installs npm dependencies in that resolved bridge directory (`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py:523-562`), so its `node_modules` is on the persistent mirror.
- The official image sets `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data` and declares `/opt/data` as its volume (`Dockerfile:294-336`); the supplied Compose file mounts the host Hermes directory there (`docker-compose.yml:36-37`).
- Regression coverage confirms the read-only-tree mirror behavior and retains an existing `node_modules` directory (`tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_bridge_dir_resolution.py:47-120`).

The timeline cross-reference to #21710 was also reviewed; that issue addressed related Docker WhatsApp bootstrap/disable behavior separately.
